utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning to you, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam, and good morning to you, as I said. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down and good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, and also good morning to my learned friends from the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I am here together with co-counsel Patricia Sellers, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our acting case manager, Ms. Sanja Bokulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. I have with me here my legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Later on today I hope to be able to sign the Nikolic certification decision. All right. Thank you. So let's bring the witness in. I think you have to draw down the curtains, Madam Usher. The air in here is unbelievable. The moment I walk in the place I start ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome back. We are going to proceed with your testimony. Madam Vidovic will go and today will be devoted entirely for the rest of the examination-in-chief. Thank you. One other thing. Please try -- you are a good witness, in other words, you don't get lost in giving descriptions that you are not asked to give or details that you are not asked to give in a question. Please try to remain like -- stay like that. Please try to be as concise as possible in your answers. Basically my advice to witnesses is to answer the question, the whole question, and nothing but the question. It will insure that you will leave this place according to schedule and not stay here beyond the end of the week up to the weekend. It depends very much on you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I will ask you about the defence of Konjevic Polje in greater detail now. Yesterday you mentioned the fact that there were about a hundred rifles there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For a while, Your Honour, could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Madam Vidovic. We are going into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did the group of Ejub Golic keep under its control the entire area of Bljecava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Ejub Golic only had an area of Bljecava under him. That was the village of Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was Golic ever the deputy of the leader of the group in Bljecava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I know Ejub Golic very well, I can tell you that he always acted independently, autonomously.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there people from other areas in Ejub's group, apart from those from Glogova?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that other people joined Ejub Golic from the village of Pale, and I believe a smaller group of people from Bljecava also joined him so that there were people who were not local.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of all the Muslim groups active in the territory of the municipality of Bratunac, as far as you know which was the largest and strongest group, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the municipality of Bratunac, Ejub Golic's group was the strongest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sir, please may I remind you of what I told you yesterday, to allow a brief interval after Ms. Vidovic's question before you answer because we need that for technical purposes and also to give as much assistance as we can to the interpreters who have to translate into English and French. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just like to raise the issue. I believe we are in private session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we are not. We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Are we in open session? Thank you. Because I wanted to state for the record that some of the people we are talking about are well-known people who many people could know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- who many people could know. And because of that we do have to be cautious about the witness's particular knowledge of someone as opposed to his knowledge that many people could have knowledge of the characteristics. I would like to say the Prosecution would like to stay in open session as much as possible, allowing for the protective measures that this witness has been granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, certainly. The protective measures that have been put in place will be observed, and you know that quite well. And in fact, that is one of the reasons why I invited Ms. Vidovic, who was very cooperative, to return back to open session when I thought it was a case of returning to open session. We ought to be in private session only when the information sought from the witness is likely or is probable to expose his identity or to reveal his identity, otherwise I think we need to stay in open session. And I think Ms. Vidovic is fully aware of that. She's been cooperative. So let's proceed. And, Witness, please allow the short interval of time, as I suggested. Thank you. Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of all the group leaders in the area, as far as you know, who had -- who enjoyed most respect among the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Ejub Golic with his people from Glogova who was held in highest esteem.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason? Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ejub Golic did most to protect his people, those who were expelled from Glogova to -- towards Bljecava and Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could I have the usher's assistance now in showing witness D812. This is a document by the municipality of Bratunac, that's to say, by the Presidency, dated 30th June, 1993, entitled "certificate," signed by the commander of the armed forces Bratunac, Ejub Golic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will quote from a small portion of this document. "Certificate." The second paragraph of the document reads: "Ibrahim Imamovic was killed in the military action in Glogova." Signed by the commander of the armed forces Bratunac, Ejub Golic. I want to ask you the following, Witness: According to what you know, was Ejub Golic appointed commander of the armed forces in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We officially learned of his appointment in early 1993, that's to say in January.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you personally come to know this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever a civilian managed to reach Konjevic Polje while in search for food, we would learn that. He -- the person involved in turn would find that out from superiors, that is, group leaders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to Bego Uminovic [as interpreted] ever about this matter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I talked to Bego Muminovic, and he told me that Ejub Golic was appointed the commander of the armed forces in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you how he came to know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As long as the road between Konjevic Polje and Cizmici was blocked, most of the information we learnt was from civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document says "armed forces Bratunac." Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this actually meant, what this was all about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bratunac armed forces formed part of Konjevic Polje, Cizmici, Bljecava, in that the people in Bljecava, as far as I heard, did not want to join Ejub Golic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These armed forces in general, what were they like? Were they uniformed? Were they armed? Did they have the necessary equipment and barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had neither the equipment nor weapons. I told you how many weapons there were in the area of Konjevic Polje. People were organised in groups, and they did not have any barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did these groups from Konjevic Polje accept Ejub Golic as a leader of theirs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did, but their communication was non-existent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of a meeting attended by someone like Bego Muminovic or someone else at which Ejub Golic and the command in general were discussed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about the meeting, but I did not learn about what the meeting discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will go back now to the events that took place in the course of the summer and autumn of 1992. You described fierce attacks from Kravica and Milici area on the Konjevic Polje area in the course of 1992. If the Serb forces attacked a village, therefore if the Serb forces attacked any of the villages in the Konjevic Polje area, what would happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every village were there was a group of this sort, and if this village came under an attack, then a member of the group would immediately try to inform other members of the group or join them in order to jointly defend the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we just go into private session for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Ms. Vidovic. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I wanted to ask you something about the 16th Muslim Brigade. Did that brigade at any point come to Konjevic Polje, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 16th Muslim Brigade came to Konjevic Polje in early August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who commanded the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was headed by Nurif Rizvanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where they were billeted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having come to Konjevic Polje, Nurif Rizvanovic, with his soldiers, was billeted next to the school. They had some tents and some of them were inside the school, but most of the school was occupied by the refugees. There was some other soldiers as well who were from Konjevic Polje itself, and they left to their homes or the homes of their relatives.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember how many fighters of the 16th Muslim Brigade came alongside Nurif Rizvanovic to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't know the precise numbers, but anywhere between 350 and 400.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were they in uniforms and armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They wore uniforms and had arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did Nurif Rizvanovic come to Konjevic Polje -- or rather, when he came, did you know any of his soldiers? Did you see some of those that came with him and that you knew them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew some of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of his soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I tried to speak with several of his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Doing so did you manage to learn anything more about Nurif Rizvanovic? For example, what he used to do before the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the outbreak of the war, Nurif Rizvanovic, if you mean the outbreak of the war in Bosnia, then I know Nurif Rizvanovic was in Croatia fighting on the Croat, or rather, Catholic side. He had a group of his own and then moved towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When Nurif Rizvanovic came to the area of Konjevic Polje, were there any female fighters amongst his ranks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember in particular one woman. She had some insignia on her sleeve. I believe it said "Croatian army."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you remember, did you ever hear her speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since I spent eight months in Croatia working and I can distinguish the way they speak, it seemed to me that she was from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to put a photograph in front of the witness. Your Honours, together with these documents I wanted to tender the letter by Mr. Omerovic, Fahrudin, who forwarded these photographs, and he expressed his willingness to testify, should it be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, for that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a look at photograph number 3. Do you have that photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise either of these two people, either personally or from having seen them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know one of the guys because when they came to Konjevic Polje I seemed to notice more the people who had two types of insignia on their sleeves.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the person on photograph number 3 who's on the left or on the right side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person on the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at the insignia that this man is wearing on his sleeve, the lower one. Could you tell the Chamber what sort of a patch this is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On his left arm one can clearly see the coat of arms and it says "Croatian army."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the insignia used by the Croatian army, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The coat of arms is -- was the same used by the HVO and HOS, but one can see here that is actually HV, that is Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned the patch that the woman wore. Was it the same kind of patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you the following: Did you see any other people amongst Nurif's soldiers who had these patches? Were there several of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw five to six of such people. There may have been more, but I saw five or six, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please assign an exhibit number to the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do I understand you well, Ms. Vidovic, because in this folder that you gave us, apart from Mr. Fahrudin's certificate, there are three photos. Do you want to tender the three of them or just photo number 3 that you have made use of?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All three of them could be put under the same exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So for the record --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right. I would just like to have clarification. Has the witness testified to the other two photographs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. But usually we have adopted the practice to admit the document just the same on the assumption that the other two photos will be made use of later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's how I have always understood it to be. But if you have an objection, then we can restrict the tendering to photo number 3 now and then proceed later with tendering the other two.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection. I understand for expediency sake, but just to clarify at this time period, this witness has not testified to the other two photos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The other two photos have not been put to the witness. So for the record, the following document is being entered into the records, consisting of three photos numbered 1, 2, and 3, respectively on the right side -- on the right side, and two sheets of paper, one in B/C/S and one in English, being a translation into English, with no ERN number, dated 28th of September, 2005, signed in Tuzla by Fahrudin Omerovic and certifying as to the identity of the individuals shown in photos 1 and 2 but certifying also that the two individuals shown in photo number 3 that was put to the witness are unknown to the same Mr. Fahrudin. This document is being tendered and received and marked as D -- defence 9 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 919. Thank you. Yes, Judge Brydensholt has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: I can see that those photographs has been taken in a place named Banovici. Could you tell us where is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Witness, please, again try to not give information that would identify you. I told you yesterday. Yes, that will be redacted. And Judge Eser has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Witness, just to make sure with regard to the photo we have seen, there are two insignia. Now, my question is: The people who had patches like this, did they, all of them, have these two insignia? Or was it that some would have one insignia and the other would have a different one? Was it always two together or would some people have only one of these insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Among the Nurif's fighters there -- some people wore two patches, the HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina patches, but only those who accompanied Nurif Rizvanovic to the Croatian battlefield. Those who were in Bosnia-Herzegovina joined the group in Tuzla before coming to Konjevic Polje, and they only had the patch of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, just one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Eser. And thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, may I offer a clarification, Your Honours. I will be using all three photographs today, but for practical reasons I asked for one exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the people who belonged to the Croatian armed forces before the outbreak of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, were they known under the name of "Zenga"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard them being called Zengas on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss these patches with anyone? Did they explain to you how come those people had them on their sleeves, as you explained to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is as I explained a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to show one of the three photographs, and that is the first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a look at the photograph and tell us, do you know anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the person on the right. This is Kemo Muminovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he come to Konjevic Polje with Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He came with Nurif Rizvanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you speak with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke with Kemo as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything about the woman you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he said she came with Nurif from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding this, I have another question. Did -- were all of the people who came with Nurif, were they all Muslim or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I couldn't ask them individually or to try to learn how many Muslims actually came there, I learned from a person called Zoran or Goran that there were some people of other nationalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at photograph number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. The witness said that he heard somebody being called Zoran or Goran, which would mean that he was of different nationality.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Hajro Ljubicic from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which of the two do you have in mind on photograph 2, the person on the left or on the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person on the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he come with Nurif Rizvanovic to the area of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I was in Konjevic Polje and when they arrived, I heard Nurif tell him to command the 3rd Company. So I guess he was the commander of the that company.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You saw their uniforms. Did they all wear the same uniforms, more or less, as we saw in the photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them had the same uniforms; the patches varied, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we briefly move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to page 10. Unfortunately, this document is not paginated, but could you please count ten pages ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's page 12 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the name at number 15. This is page beginning with number 1, and under 15 there is Kemal Muminovic, son of Huso, from Mihaljevici. Did you locate the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10, you said?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a page beginning with number 1, and we were interested in number 15. It is stated here Kemal Muminovic, son of Huso, from Mihaljevici. Is that the person you said you spoke with and that that person came to Konjevic Polje with Mr. Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please go to page 4. Go to the very beginning and then four pages ahead. Can you see that? Page 4, number 11. Dubicic Hajrudin, son of Mehmedalija. In the English translation this is page 4, at the bottom almost. Hajrudin Dubicic, son of Mehmedalija. Is that the person you said you spoke with about Nurif's fighters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can remove the document now. And we will ask for another document to be given to the witness. Your Honours, as concerns D822, I wanted to distribute the original certificate of the directorate of defence of the canton of Tuzla, dated the 18th of August, 2005, and one can see that D822, as well D818, we received from the archives of the directorate. Could we please assign number 2822.1 or A to the other document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll do that, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will read a part of the document. It is entitled "armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Drina Division command," signed by the commander of the Drina Division, Nurif Rizvanovic, and I wanted to quote a portion of the document. It begins with "Mr. Ahmic. I was appointed commander of the Drina Division by decision number 1-7/92 of 5 September from municipalities of Bratunac, Zvornik, Vlasenica, and Srebrenica. In view of this, I would like to ask you to help me implement these decisions." For example: "The mass media should keep repeating the order of 9 September 1992, strictly confidential number 01/92-1, items 1(a) and (b)," and, "a stamp should be made in accordance with the decision and sent to me by a courier." First of all, I wanted to ask you, do you know who Mr. Ahmic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ahmic is from Bratunac. He was attached to a sort of staff in Tuzla, and it is probably on this matter that Nurif Rizvanovic addresses him. That was a forward post where the staff was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This forward post staff, was it from Bratunac? You mentioned Bratunac a while ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the forward post staff from Bratunac, therefore it was relocated from Bratunac -- or rather, it was a forward post in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have the usher's assistance now. This document could be removed from the witness and could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit P82.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So in the meantime, Ms. Vidovic, I'm going to docket this other document that you handed to us, which consists of one page in B/C/S, being a statement of -- listing four documents that were handed over to you by the Ministry of Defence of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Tuzla canton defence office, on the 18th of August, 2005, together with the corresponding translation thereof into English, consisting of two pages. These together are being entered and marked as Defence Exhibit D920.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I believe that you have before you a document P82. This is a document issued by the Drina Division. It's a decision dated 27 October 1992, bearing the number 02110276. First of all, do you see the date that this decision has? That's the date of 27 October 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us whether you see anyone's signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No signature has been affixed to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war you had a job, but after the war you became a professional member of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Can you tell the Trial Chamber whether it was customary for the documents, particularly decisions, to be signed in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any written document had to have a signature in addition to a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will quote the last sentence of the document which reads as follows: "The newly appointed commander Nurif Rizvanovic agreed to put himself under Naser Oric's command." Witness, you indicated on several occasions that you were in touch with Nurif's fighters. Did you hear that Nurif Rizvanovic was at any point under the command of anyone from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear that. I never heard of anyone coming from Srebrenica. I only knew about civilians. I didn't know about him meeting with anyone or agreeing to being under Naser Oric's command. No, that I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when it was that Nurif Rizvanovic left Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard, I did not see, that in early November Nurif Rizvanovic was taken somewhere - this was indicated to me by someone - that he went toward Tuzla. What actually happened, I can't say. I don't know anything about Nurif Rizvanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you heard that he had left in early November. Was this only several days after the 27th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the case. Several days later, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness be shown a different document now. This is a document by the Drina Division command dated 2nd November 1992 bearing the title "war report," signed by the commander of the Drina Division, Nurif Rizvanovic, addressed to Commander Meholjic. The document does bear the ERN number which is 02110304.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the document. I will quote a part of the document request it says: "Konjevic Polje, the 2nd of November, 1992, for commander Meholjic - war report. It is my personal honour and a great pleasure to be able to greet you, your fighters, and the doctor. As for the problems that you wrote about, I have the same problems. The wounded are the most difficult problem for me. At the moment there are 200 of them. The other issues are well-known: Medicines, ammunition, decline of morale, and other. I'm delivering you a report. The defenders of Zvornik cowardly abandoned their defence lines and most of the commanders fled. The Cerska lines were taken by the Chetniks. The lines of Konjevic Polje are stable and firm. One fierce offensive more, and I will be forced to leave the territory because of the low morale among the fighters and their commanders." Witness, do you know who is Commander Meholjic to whom Nurif Rizvanovic addresses this war report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do -- actually, I did not know at the time when I was in Konjevic Polje, but as I came to Srebrenica I learned that Akim Meholjic [as interpreted] was chief of police in Srebrenica. I found that out when I came to Srebrenica from Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find out anything about his whereabouts and what he was in -- doing in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait, wait, wait, because I know what Ms. Sellers is coming up with. It's the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, as a matter of fact it isn't the name. I have the honour to ask if we have a problem with the translation. Because I understood Madam Vidovic to read "from here that I would be forced to leave the territory." The English translation is "live." And I would like to see if we could just clarify that right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take both of them, then, one after the other. The first one is the transcript shows the name of Akim Meholjic. We don't -- we are not talking about Akim Meholjic but Hakija Meholjic. Is that correct? You never mentioned Akim but Hakija Meholjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Hakija Meholjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, the other part -- it's -- I think Ms. Vidovic will take care of that. Which part in the -- in the Bosnian text, which line would that be? Because this is all handwritten and I can decipher some of it but not all. Ms. Vidovic, can you help us, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps it will be best for me to read this briefly again. It says: "War report. It is my personal honour and great pleasure to be able to greet you, you, your fighters, and the doctor. As for the problems that you wrote about, I have the same problems. The wounded are the most difficult problem for me. At the moment there are about 200 of them. For the rest, the issues are well-known: Medicines, ammunition, decline of morale, and other matters. I'm hereby giving you the report. The defenders of Zvornik, cowardly abandoned their defence lines, and most of the commanders fled. The lines of Cerska were taken by the Chetniks. The lines of Konjevic Polje are stable and firm. One fierce offensive more, and I will be forced to leave the territory because of the low morale among the fighters and their commanders." And that's what the original says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Stop there. I think that solves the problem. It's definitely "will be forced to leave" --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and not anything else. All right. I think we have cleared that up. We can proceed. Thank you, Madam Vidovic. And thank you, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, before going back to the document I asked you whether you heard anything about the activities of Mr. Meholjic in the course of 1992 in Srebrenica. Did you hear what he was doing there, if you heard anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since Srebrenica was occupied by the Chetniks, as I arrived in Srebrenica I heard that Hakija Meholjic was the first one to enter Srebrenica with his men. And to me that meant that he had liberated Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. After Nurif Rizvanovic left Srebrenica, do you know what happened to his men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your earlier evidence you stated that you heard that Nurif Rizvanovic had left the area. My question to you was whether his fighters left the area as well or whether they remained in the area of Konjevic Polje or elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them left the area. Most of them stayed behind in Konjevic Polje. Some of them joined Ejub Golic in Cizmici, and some of them probably went along with him, but not many.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a group that stayed behind in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I have said, a larger group stayed behind in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went to the village of Grabovsko.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did this unit stay behind as an independent unit or did it join any other group? And I'm referring to the unit in Grabovsko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It continued existing as an independent group without joining any others.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who led the group in Grabovsko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Refik Hasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness be shown Defence Exhibit D801, and that's to say photograph number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. In the meantime, we need to give this last document that you used a number. And this document consisting of three handwritten pages in B/C/S with ERN 02110304 to 0306 included and a typed translation thereof into English, consisting also of three pages, is being tendered, marked as Defence Exhibit D921.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have the photograph? Photograph number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know either or both of the two on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Refik Hasanovic is on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that the person you said a while ago had replaced Nurif Rizvanovic when he left and stayed behind in Grabovsko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You can remove the photograph. I have another question in connection with this. Apart from Nurif Rizvanovic's men for whom you said the -- that they had uniforms, did the other groups in Konjevic Polje have uniforms until the -- until Konjevic Polje fell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no uniforms. We only had our civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will put to you a series of brief questions on a different topic. You've been telling us about the organisation of forces up until November 1992. Did you ever hear that in early November 1992 in Konjevic Polje a meeting was held where a decision was taken to establish something that was called a subregion? Did you ever hear anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A meeting was held, but I don't know anything specific about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of the establishment of a subregion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In early November 1992, did you notice that the situation on the ground changed in terms of the fact that Konjevic Polje was operating under Srebrenica's command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Command itself never changed. From the very beginning up until March 1993, it was organised between smaller groups. There were smaller groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to claim that the subregion was operational, that the authorities of the subregion were active and operational in the Konjevic Polje area, would that tally with what you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. That's not true at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the break, I would like the witness to be shown another document bearing the number 04337015. You can remove the photographs, please. This is a document by the Bratunac Battalion command dated --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear which date.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] September 1992, addressed to the commander of the Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will now take you back to the events which transpired in the summer and early autumn of 1992 through to the fall of Konjevic Polje. I will quote from the document. It reads: "Reply to your memo on the exact position of our units: Loznicka Rijeka, Kunjerac, Pobrdje, Mahmutovici, Borici, Trig Point 438, Kaolin, Lomenac, Pajici, Magasici, Jecila, Radukici, Jezevtica, Menjak, Siljkovici, Mratinici, Doljani, Brana, Bacici, Panjevici, Trig Point 445. Sopotnik." Signed by Colonel Dimitrije Sibanic. Witness, did you know of any of these lines held by the Serb forces, namely the lines indicated in the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know of many of these lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us specifically which lines you were aware of at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Siljkovici, then Mratinci, and then another illegible place, Brana, Bacici -- this should not be Panjevici, rather Banjevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Which of these lines were in the proximity of Urkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Siljkovici, Mratinci, Brana, Bacici, and Banjevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the map he was shown yesterday to mark the lines for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: While this is being done I'll ask you the following. The places you mentioned, namely Siljkovici, Mratinci, Brana, Bacici, Banjevici, are these hamlets of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are hamlets of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us the lines, or rather, the places.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Banjevici, Brana, Bacici, Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the area below Kravica. And I have another question in connection with this. To your knowledge -- or let me rephrase. Were you able to see whether these lines went through inhabited places themselves or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They went through inhabited places.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Ms. Vidovic. This document which consists of two pages with ERN 04337015, one in B/C/S and the other one in English, is being assigned Defence Exhibit Number D922.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this would be a good moment for a break, if you agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Madam Vidovic, and it needs to be 30 minutes because of the redaction.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, could I ask that if the witness could leave the room, and prior to us breaking I would just like to put something on the record for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The thing is we'll have to draw down the curtains before he does that because there are people in the gallery. They don't need to leave -- you don't need to leave, because in any case we will still have to draw the curtains down because of cameras and everything. I think the witness can be escorted out of the courtroom now -- yeah, yeah, they are not going to recognise him from his shoes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would like to draw the Trial Chamber's and the Defence's attention to the fact that this witness has testified fairly extensively within this session on the actions, the duties of Nurif Rizvanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the effect that that has on relevant issues of command and control, very relevant issues also of what groups took part in what battles, and now relationships between Mr. -- or Commander Rizvanovic and a Prosecution witness. The Defence has fulfilled their obligations, as was seen priorly, in submitting a summary of the possible evidence that a witness should give. When the Prosecution is in the position of not thinking the summary is sufficient, we send correspondence. In this case we sent a letter asking if there were any other areas and some specific questions. And Defence responded to our letter that they would not be elaborating on the summary for the purposes of this witness. And we, the Prosecution, accepted that your summary must have been complete from your point of view. We still think the summary wasn't complete, and now after the witness has testified and gone into a very important area that has been within the Prosecution's pre-trial brief, that has been within other evidence, we do have not only the subregion being brought up, which is not in the summary, but also Commander Rizvanovic. Your Honour, I would ask two things: That the summaries that Defence gives, particularly if it changes during proofing, that the Prosecution be updated as to the areas and the evidence that they intend to lead. The second thing I would have to ask in this case, because it is substantial, and I will say there is a de minimus part of that, that means that our cross-examination certainly must address some of these issues. Since we are only apparently halfway through this witness's testimony, that will not pose enormous problems, but I would just like to alert the Trial Chamber that the contents of the summary certainly relates to our ability to prepare for cross-examination and that actual preparation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Your comments, Ms. Vidovic, before we give our own.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. We have provided on this specific occasion a very detailed summary, which included the events of the defence of Konjevic Polje. At least two of us -- of our previous witnesses, whenever mentioning Konjevic Polje, undoubtedly also extensively testified about Nurif Rizvanovic. Whoever investigated Konjevic Polje and the defence thereof, wherever there was mention of Konjevic Polje, it could not have come as a surprise to the Prosecutor that this was -- would immediately be linked up with Nurif Rizvanovic's name. Besides, they dealt extensively with Nurif Rizvanovic in their pre-trial brief. There is nothing that comes as a surprise or as something new in what the witness testified so far. We indicated that the witness was going to testify about Konjevic Polje, and I therefore believe that we have fully honoured our obligation. Of course, Your Honour, until the witness comes, until we talk to him shortly before his testimony, we are unable to know all the details that the witness will state. You have to know that the summaries were done in a very short span of time this summer. You have to know that we never talked to a group of witnesses, including this particular witness, we never talked to him prior to meeting him here. I believe that we were quite fair in providing pretty detailed summaries. I was expecting this objection because we had correspondence with the OTP. I checked the case law concerning Defence teams in other cases, and I must say that the summaries provided there were far less concise -- or rather, I wanted to say that they were far shorter, less detailed, in all these other cases. If I indicate that the witness is to testify about the events in Konjevic Polje, then anyone who had to do anything with Konjevic Polje, had analysed Konjevic Polje would know that it would also involve Nurif Rizvanovic. I do not believe that we have breached any of our obligations, especially not the one under Rule 65 ter (G).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I thank you, Madam Vidovic. Your final comments, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate the observations of Defence counsel, but I would say that in this instance whenever they have brought witnesses before Your Honours who would testify about the subregion, that was always stated clearly in their summary. And in this time we have a summary in which that is not stated. So while Konjevic Polje certainly could always imply the subregion, this time it was not there, as if it was specifically not an area that we were going to go into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, before we come back to you on this, between the filing of the Defence witness summaries that we got way back in August, which are the only summaries that we have, did you ever receive anything else in relation to this document from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We are working from the same summaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That's why a time prior to a witness coming forward, we enter into correspondence with our learned friends to ask will there be other information that we can have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure of that. In other words, after the arrival of the witness here in The Hague and his briefing or proofing by the Defence, you have not received anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, the Defence never provides that spontaneously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We'll come back to you after the break on this. Thank you. We'll have a 30-minute break starting from now, which basically means we'll reconvene at five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. With the -- with -- pardon? No, no, no, it's -- they have started transmitting. You need to press video monitor once more and it should come. So basically let's deal with the matter that Ms. Sellers raised before the break. We do appreciate, Ms. Vidovic, for sure that when we ask you to submit Defence witness summaries, these are necessarily restricted to what is within your knowledge at the time. So we don't expect you to foresee other matters that might be dealt with by -- by the witness when he or she eventually comes over. But we have the practice here of proofing the witness before giving evidence, and it is usually the case that during this proofing there are issues that you find out the witness will be able to cover. And the most obvious -- you may sit down, please, make yourself comfortable. And the most obvious evidence of this is that while in the summary you would have told us roughly you need 3.5 hours for that witness's statement. As we have been going along after the proofing, sometimes that figure doubles, as has been also in this case. So what we are asking is the following: There is some validity to what you have suggested, that when you indicated in the summary that the witness will be dealing with Konjevic Polje, one would have expected that the name of Nurif Rizvanovic would have come up. I think it's fair to say that I would have expected the witness to at least mention, but to go into all the details that he did. So at that point in time, once the proofing has been made, has been finished, and you are in a position to put it in juxtaposition with the summary that you would have provided, I think if not for any other reasons but at least for courtesy and the good environment that we have tried to secure the relationship between the Prosecution and the Defence in this case would appreciate it if you indicate areas which the witness will be covering beyond what one would expect reading the summary. I have to agree with Ms. Sellers. We -- none of us in fact were expecting reading the Defence witness summary that the Defence witness summary will also be dealing with, for example, command and control issues in Konjevic Polje in relation to Nurif or with regard to the regional set-up. So let's try -- I know that it is not easy. I know that the kind of hours that we work here and the pressure that we have and the stress that is involved by having to work on Saturdays and on Sundays to proof witnesses carries with it its weight and -- I mean, it's stressful for everyone, but let's try to cooperate a little bit more, all right, and so that we don't have to waste five minutes or ten minutes in future having to deal with such matters. Ms. Sellers, I think, is right in complaining that to an extent she has been surprised in some -- with the mentioning of some elements or issues. And of course I have to -- I barely need to put your mind at rest that you will be given all the opportunity to address these issues during your cross-examination. I mean, it's no point in even doubting -- doubting that. All right. Do you get my message, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I did get your message. I expect that such letters and inquiries will be forwarded to us in a fair manner, just as you put it. If we receive this in -- by way of an order or in an unfair way, then we will only do what we are bound to do. I don't want to trouble you more with that, but the reason why I thought the OTP had sufficient information was that in item 3 of the summary we precisely stated that the witness will testify with regard to paragraph 7, which is the accused's command over Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik. And paragraph 7 of the indictment deals with the exact area of the subregion. Paragraph 7 of the indictment mentions the accused's command responsibility over the subregion; that's why I didn't think that would be a surprise. But in any case, I received your message and I will act accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you -- thank you both.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And your cooperation in this area, your further cooperation, because I must say -- I must state publicly that all in all, all in all, I have no complaints. I mean, I think you have cooperated to a large extent so far, and I must commend you for that. In the future, if you could possibly avoid further incidents like this, I think we would all benefit from that. Yes, let's continue with the witness, Ms. Vidovic, and we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to put another document in front of the witness. This is a Bratunac garrison command number 04337001 dated 8 October 1992. This is a report to brigade commander signed by garrison commander Captain Vaso Gujic. I will quote a part of the document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Item 1: "Forces attacking Urkovici encountered fierce resistance. One of our men was killed. The troops withdrew to the initial positions. "Ambushes were laid to infiltrate troops into Srebrenica. We will additionally reinforce the ambushes. "By tomorrow, we will reinforce an additional line towards Banjevici. "When the circumstances allow for this, the air force will attack tomorrow. One (Kraguj) airplane is available."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, by all means, Ms. Vidovic. Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Are you finished with this document, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not yet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in item 2 of the document ambushes are mentioned. Do you remember where those ambushes were laid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They usually took place between Siljkovici towards Konjevic Polje at the area called Buljim. Along that axis we encountered ambushes most frequently. Those were the fighters from Milici and Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those were Serb fighters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were Serb fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why were those ambushes laid, against whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ambushes were laid because these were the routes used by civilians the most and that's where they usually got killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why did the civilians use that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went in search of food.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the situation with food in Konjevic Polje, if you can explain it to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation was grave in Konjevic Polje, and it was even graver in Srebrenica because we occasionally would receive some information from the people who came from there to the territory of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please assign an exhibit number to this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic. This document which consists of two pages, one in B/C/S and the other one being the corresponding translation of it into English with ERN 04337001 is being assigned Defence Exhibit Number D923.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to put another document in front of the witness. This is a document from the Drina Corps command. It is a Drina Corps command document dated 4 November 1992. The ERN number is 04292136. The title of the document is "Order on final stage of combat operations."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I wanted to quote the first three paragraphs of the document. "After months of combat operations conducted in the territory of Zvornik, Sekovici, Vlasenica, Milici, Bratunac, we have entered the final stage of combat operations. "The enemy has been pushed into a very small area" -- the document actually states -- the document has been actually pushed in a small room, as it is stated in B/C/S, but it should be area "with Konjevic Polje at its centre and is completely surrounded and facing a total military defeat." "With the liberation of this territory, combat operations in it will stop and we shall gain invaluable free territory and reinforce our positions towards Tuzla, Kalesija, Kladanj, and Srebrenica." Witness, on the 4th of November, 1992, the Drina Corps commander, Milenko Zivanovic, reports on the final stage of combat operations pertaining to Konjevic Polje. The three paragraphs I read, does it reflect the situation on the ground in the sense that the Muslims were pushed into a very small area with Konjevic Polje at its centre and was completely surrounded on the 4th of November, 1992? Does that tally with what one could experience in Konjevic Polje at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The document clearly portrays and proves the situation, and that was the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that what your experience was like there at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will continue quoting some other statements from the document. First and foremost, was it your impression at the time that Konjevic Polje was completely surrounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our impression was that Konjevic Polje was completely surrounded and there were situations in which we were unable to help each other. We fought to the bitter end.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to quote item 7 of the document. It states: "The areas of responsibility for the units for final clearing up work and territorial control are as follows: A, the Drinjaca Zelinje battalion, Kuslat village, Konjevici village." As regards this, I wanted to ask you the following. In your knowledge, is it correct that Konjevici Polje were attacked from the area of Zelinje in early November 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at subitem (b) on the next page. "The Kravica Battalion, Urkovici village, Hrncici village, Konjevic Polje." Do you remember and is it correct that on the 4th November, 1992, and the days after that, Hrncici, Urkovici, and Konjevic Polje were attacked from the direction of Kravica, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct, because when they were attacking Hrncici and Urkovici, they were also shelling the centre of Konjevic Polje. And it seems that based on this document they thought it would suffice to take over that territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that on the 4th of November, 1992, that area was under attack from the area of Kravica? Was it your experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I just said that a minute ago, when I was in Urkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we give an exhibit number to this document, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Ms. Vidovic. This document which consists of three pages in Serbo-Croat, two of which are typewritten and one of which is handwritten, and three corresponding pages all typed, being the translation thereof into English is being tendered, received, and marked as Defence Exhibit D924.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we will show you another document. This is a Drina Corps command document dated on the 4th of November, 1992 as well, signed by Commander Colonel Milenko Zivanovic, the number being 04293122. It is a short document. I will read out the entire contents: "On 5 November 1992, starting at 7.00 p.m., a working meeting will take place in Siljkovici. You, the brigade commander, and your immediate subordinates, the battalion commanders of Vlasenica, Bratunac, Drinjaca, and Milici, and the 6th Battalion of Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade shall attend the meeting. "You are to come to the working meeting with proposals for the execution of the final actions in Konjevic Polje in your area of responsibility." My question, hence, is the following: Did you have any knowledge about the ensuing attack, a large attack, by the Serbs to finally break through the resistance lines of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, one moment. Let's see -- is this an objection?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. So we can make sure that the record is clear. Madam Vidovic stated in the description of the document that it was signed by colonel Milenko Zivanovic, and when I look at the original B/C/S I certainly see his name there, but I do not see a signature indicated. And in assistance of not only identifying the document but certainly we don't want the witness to think there was a signature on the document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think that's a fair point made by Ms. Sellers. Witness, it's not being put to you that this is signed by Mr. -- or Colonel Milenko Zivanovic, but the paternity of this document is being attributed to him, this notwithstanding. I suppose you agree to this, Ms. Vidovic? And let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. It is obviously a dispatch, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But in any case, thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I wanted to ask you the following: You, the people in that area, were you able to sense that the final stage of attacks was to take place against Konjevic Polje on the 5th of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could see, as well as those around me who could observe with the naked eye and the binoculars we had, one could clearly see that large numbers of people were on the move in the villages and that the tanks and the APCs are getting ready, those standing next to Milo Milanovic's house, as well as in other villages. So quite a number of soldiers grouped and we could foresee a strong offensive against us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we assign an exhibit number to this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic, this document is being assigned Defence Exhibit Number D925, consists of two pages, one in B/C/S, on in English with ERN 04293122.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask that another document be shown to the witness. This is a document from the command of the Drina Corps dated the 20th November 1992, the ERN number being 04361528. This is a document forwarding some information. At the end of the document, we can see the name of Commander Lieutenant Colonel Borivoje Tesic. I will read out the entire document to the witness. I would kindly ask him to pay attention. "The Konjevic Polje-Srebrenica route has been cut off along the Zabrdje-Jasikovaca line since 14 November 1992. "The valley towards Hajducko Groblje can be controlled from the Siljkovici feature. The troops chosen to close the line are from the 3rd Battalion (commander is Mile Milovanovic, reserve Captain) and from the Derventa Battalion. 35 troops from three battalions of my unit were chosen to close the line; their commander is Milan Ivanovic and the company commander is Rocko Peric. They are only armed with personal weapons. There is an anti-aircraft machine-gun on Siljkovici. The area can be controlled with an 82-millimetre mortar. We will provide preparatory fire. Obstacles must be laid in part of the area on 21 November 1992."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, as regards this document, will you please answer the following: According to your knowledge, what was actually the direction of Zabrdje and Jasikovaca. Who used that direction, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zabrdje-Jasikovaca, that is the road from Kravica -- or rather, the hamlet of Siljkovici towards Milici. That was the route controlled by the Serbs and they laid an ambush there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your knowledge, did the Muslim civilians try to use that route in their search of food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the route used to reach Konjevic Polje and the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you point Zabrdje and Jasikovaca on the map for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The map needs to be adjusted on the ELMO properly because we can't follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, it is close to your finger, a bit to the left upwards near Zabrdje. You have pointed the place. Could you please mark it off. It was right under your finger a moment ago. It's a bit down from your pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jasikovaca and Zabrdje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. To your knowledge at this point in time, in mid-November 1992, was this route cut off, thus making it impossible for the civilians to move in the area in search of food or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time it was completely cut off. Nobody was able to go to or from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is stated here that from the Siljkovici feature one could command the valley in the direction of Hajducko Groblje and that the forces charged with this are from the ranks of the 3rd Battalion. Is it true that at this time the villages surrounding Siljkovici as well as Siljkovici itself was targeted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. The surrounding Muslim villages were targeted from Siljkovici, whereas artillery targeted Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the existence of this anti-aircraft machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. One could see it clearly next to a Howitzer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of the 3rd Battalion in November 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about the battalion in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where did the battalion come from, according to what you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a Kravica battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be assigned a number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. This document, which consists of two pages, one in Serbo-Croat, the other one in English, being a translation, bearing ERN 04361528, in both cases, is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D926.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will show you another document by the Bratunac Brigade command dated the 24 November 1992, the ERN number being 04361531. I will quote the document. "For the purpose of commander's reconnaissance to be carried out together with subordinate officers, herein you will find the working points in the brigade's area of responsibility for the execution of the task at hand: "1. Working point-1, Banjevici village (Lupoglava). "2. Working point-2, Siljkovici village." Based on your service in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, can you tell us what "working point" means.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Working point means assigning combat operations, or rather, distributing combat operations from this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on your knowledge and experience from the area, did your villages come under attack in mid-November 1992 from Banjevici and Siljkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These villages were practically never left alone. They were constantly under attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Vidovic, before you proceed. Let me take you back to your Exhibit D922, which was tendered and admitted this morning. There we had the term [B/C/S spoken] and here we have "radna tacka." Can the witness explain the difference, please. One was translated to us as trig point. The [B/C/S spoken] was trigonometric combination, and it's called trig point. This one is given another name,"radna tacka," so perhaps one could enlighten us on where the distinction lies. This is a working point. How is it arrived at? Because I think it would be of some importance to us. Have you understood me? You were in the army, you should know a little bit about this, so...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Working point is the point where senior officers meet, like commanders of battalions or brigades, even possibly company commanders, and in that area they are assigned different locations to which their units will move and where they will launch attacks. As for the trigonometric point, I am less familiar with the term. I believe that refers to the line that is closest to where the attack takes place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see -- I see your --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see your client disagreeing with this, so I don't know if you want to pursue it any further with the witness now. You may of course do so. But I noticed the accused disagreeing. And I am not qualified enough on the subject to intervene and explain why one is different from the other. No, I don't want to hear your client, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, trigonometric point is a geographic term which shows -- or rather, denotes a certain elevation. It is more of a geographical term than a military one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that's how it was mentioned in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. To me it's the meeting point of two or more, usually three, coordinates. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Exactly, coordinates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed then.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you can remember, was the Konjevic Polje area attacked on around the 24th of November, 1992 as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already indicated that it was under attack even before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it attacked from the area of Siljkovici and Banjevici, that's to say, from the hamlets of Kravica, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those were the directions from which most of the attacks came, therefore from the Kravica Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be assigned a number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document, which consists of two pages, one in B/C/S, and one in English, the English being a translation of the former one, is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D927. The ERN number is 04361531.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher now to show the witness another Drina Corps document, also dated 24 November 1992. And it says "very urgent, decision for further action." And I will quote while it is being distributed. "Pursuant to the directive of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, strictly confidential, number 02/3 of 19 November 1992 and based on an assessment of the situation, I have decided: "Launch an attack using the main body of troops and major equipment to inflict on the enemy the highest possible losses, exhaust them, break them up or force them to surrender, and force the local Muslim population to abandon the area of Cerska, Zepa, Srebrenica, and Gorazde. Liberate and render usable the Milici-Konjevic Polje-Zvornik road and open the corridor towards eastern Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned the intensity of the attacks around the 24th of November, 1992 targeting Konjevic Polje. Could you on the basis of that conclude that the Serbs were trying to force the Muslim population to abandon the Podrinje area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
