utterances.text: Yes. It was concluded that way, and our conclusion was 100 per cent that; however, we stood ground, resisted the attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the terminology used here "to force them to surrender, to force the local Muslim population to abandon the area of Cerska, Zepa," and on the basis of what you were able to see and experience in November 1992 on the ground, can you infer that the Serbs were already planning at the time to do what in fact happened in the area in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I could have inferred that because in addition to all this they were throwing flyers off planes telling us to surrender and surrender our weapons. Right after that, fierce attacks ensued. What we were able to conclude on the basis of these flyers that were distributed and the rest was in fact proved by the events in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now read to you from a different portion of this document. Please turn to page 2, paragraph 2. It says: "In the first stage lasting 20 to 30 days, crush the enemy forces or force them to surrender unconditionally in the sectors of Cerska, Konjevic Polje, and Zepa, and directly put up a blockade at Olovo." My question to you is: Within some 20 to 30 days after the 24th of November, 1992, did there ensue even fiercer attacks against Konjevic Polje or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Shortly after these flyers were thrown off planes, attacks were launched against Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this in the course of December 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were these artillery attacks or not? What was the intensity of these attacks? Could you briefly tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were artillery attacks where mortars were engaged, APCs, tanks, Howitzers, anti-aircraft cannons, and various other weapons, and of course infantry forces were engaged as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did it happen sometime in December 1992 that there was someone counting the shells that landed in the area on a particular day in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given that there was a lot of shelling on the area -- in the area before, there was a lady, if I can say who she was, she was Muminovic, Bego's wife, her name was Fata who started counting shells, and she counted them up to a thousand, and perhaps when she stopped counting, there may have been some 70 more.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have almost finished with this document. Please look at 2.2 of the document where it is stated: "The Bratunac Light Brigade used the main body of troops to launch an attack to break up enemy forces and reach the features of Loznik, Zanik Caus, and Bijela Stijena use the remaining forces to cut the Srebrenica-Cerska road in coordination with part of the Birac Brigade and the Milici Battalion, and then in coordination with the Birac and the Zvornik Brigades, liberate Pobudje, Hrncici, and Konjevic Polje and thus create conditions to open the Vlasenica-Milici-Drinjaca road." Pay specific, please, attention to the following paragraph: "Consolidate the Fakovici Battalion as soon as possible and give it the task of penetrating as deep as possible into the area of Srebrenica using the territory of Serbian villages and attack Srebrenica from there." Witness, is it true, based on what you were able to observe and experience, that Serb villages were used as venues from which the surrounding Muslim villages were attacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb villages had always been used for the purpose of attacking Muslim areas. This document states that the Cerska-Srebrenica road should be severed, which shows and proves that the entire Konjevic Polje area should be cleansed in order to be able to link up with Cerska. There was no other way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, the drift of my question was quite different. I quoted to you a portion of the document which says that the territory of the Serb villages is used for launching attacks against Muslim areas. Based on your experience in Podrinje or specifically in the area where you were residing, can you tell us whether Serb villages were used as venues from which attacks were launched on Muslim areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, this document which consists of six pages, three of which are in B/C/S, the other three in English, being a translation, with ERN 04292352 to 354, page included, is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D928.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will show you another document now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher show the witness a Drina Corps command document dated 12 December 1992, bearing the number 04358084, addressed to the commands of the Zvornik, Birac, and Bratunac Brigade, and so on. The document states: "Very urgent. Order on taking measures to defend from military intervention of foreign countries against Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at point 2 [as interpreted] of the order on the second page where it is stated: "Brigade commands and, if necessary, battalion commands, should be deployed in the basements of massive buildings while undertaking measures to prevent a decrease in efficiency of management and command." My question to you is as follows: Are you surprised by what this document states that the Serbs located their headquarters in massive buildings? Did you know of any headquarters in buildings which were not military features but were quite massive in their construction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told you that I know very well what the school in Kravica was like. There was a new building and an old one. I also knew about this field above the Bacici dam where there was another building. These were the two buildings that could be used for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The transcript says that these two buildings could be used for that purpose. Was it the case that they could be used or were they in fact used by the army? Did the army use them as headquarters, as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stated on several occasions that this was indeed the case, they were used for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This was just to clarify the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the document be assigned a Defence exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document which equally consists of three pages in English and three pages in B/C/S with ERN 04358084 to 086 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D929. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I noted that Madam Vidovic said please look at point 2. I believe she might have wanted to say look at point 4 of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I heard her say page 2, not point 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Then we might need to just correct the transcript which inadvertently picked up point 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let me search it. Yes, yes, yes, the transcript definitely needs to be corrected. In line 20 of the previous page it says point 2 of the order on the second page. It should read "point 4 of the order on the second page." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe the witness already has the document by the Bratunac Brigade command dated 5 January 1993 bearing the number 04359300. This is the order by the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, Lieutenant Colonel Milan Urosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will quote to you item 3: "I hereby order all weapons and ammunition that was distributed to individuals before the establishment of the armed forces of the Serb Republic which are not used and are kept in houses to be returned. The weapons are to be returned to the brigade command by the 10th of January, 1993."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In connection with this, Your Honour, could we move into private session for a while, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's move into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, this document which consists of two pages the ERN 04359300, one in B/C/S, one in English, is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D930.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the map now. Could you point to the location of Zelinje for Their Honours. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how large the village is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't really large.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the area of Konjevic Polje attacked from Zelinje in the period between -- starting in 1992 until its fall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was mostly from Zelinje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to Konjevic Polje itself rather than the surrounding area when you say that the attacks mostly came from Zelinje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These troops were attacking Konjevici and Banjevici together with Drinjaca -- with Drinjaca command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like the usher to show the witness a document dated 24 November 1992 issued by the brigade command -- Bratunac Brigade command bearing the number 04361530, which is a document addressed to the command of the Drina Corps. I will quote from items 1 and 2 of the document, wherein it is stated: "The Zelinje Company was resubordinated to my brigade. "The commander of the Zelinje Company is Radosav Milosevic, the commander of the Sopotnik Company is Slavoljub Vidakovic and the commander of the part of the Zeljova forces is Nikola Mitrovic." It is handwritten here: "The forces resubordinated to me are 154 strong." It is stated below: "They are armed with: PM submachine-gun, M-84 two pieces; PM M-72, 7.62 millimetre, 13 pieces; PM M-53, two pieces; automatic rifles, 56 pieces; semi-automatic rifles, 69 pieces; and submachine-guns, 12 pieces." Witness, you stated that Zelinje was not a large village. According to this document, one could conclude Zelinje Company had 17 light machine-guns. Can you tell the Trial Chamber whether a light machine-gun is a dangerous piece of weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The M-72 light machine-gun dates from 1972 that I used during my military service and it has a much longer range than an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that a dangerous weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The longer the range, the more dangerous the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your experience, the Serb villages around Konjevic Polje, were they all armed or not, if you have any knowledge as to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will probably be mistaken if I said that not every single one of them was armed. They were all armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What do you base your conclusion on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because all of the villages that I was able to notice had military troops there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From your testimony so far, did I understand probably that not only trenches were used to open fire at Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have much use of trenches. They felt strong and they thought they would be able to deal with the entire situation from their houses rather than from trenches.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we assign an exhibit number to the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document, which consists of one page in B/C/S, and two pages in English, with ERN 04361530 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D931.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we give another document to the witness. This is another Bratunac Brigade command dated 27 November 1992, the ERN number being 04363003. The name of Lieutenant Colonel Borivoje Tesic appears and it was sent to the Drina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, while you're waiting for the document I wanted to quote item 4 of the text. It states: "At about 1200 hours, three vehicles, out of which two cars and a lorry, set off for Kravica. For yet-unestablished reasons, the two last vehicles missed the turning for Kravica and continued straight on. In the Sandici sector they entered among the Muslims. The lorry was destroyed." Further down under item 7 it states: "The lorry carried 80, 120-millimetre mortar shells, 40 Zoljas, eight Maljutkas, and three M-84 machine-guns. They were all destroyed, and the lorry was set on fire by Muslims' incendiary ammunition."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we move shortly into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's move into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document bearing ERN 04363003, both in the English and in the original Serbo-Croat text, consisting of two pages, which -- one in each of the two said languages, is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D932.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at some other documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask that D819 be given to the witness. This is a Bratunac Brigade command document dated 4 December 1992. The title being "Decision to attack." I wanted to quote item 4. It states: "I have decided to regroup and bring in some of the brigade forces along the Bratunac-Kravica-Banjevici village axis and then from an initial position right: Sopotnik village left excluding the group of houses in Gornja Brana village, move on to the attack grouping main forces on the Lupoglava (Banjevici village) Konjic (667)-Drenjak (trig point 771)-elevation overlooking Konjevic Polje axis."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn the page. On page 2, item 6 it states in the second paragraph: "Use a frontal attack and combine action in the first and third JGs to destroy the Muslim forces on the axis of attack. Having broken out on to the Haluge feature, create conditions to consolidate the forces of our brigade's 3rd Battalion." Further down it states: "Support 82-millimetre mortar from the Lupoglava sector, self-propelled gun from Goli Vis." In your testimony you stated that the 3rd Battalion was from Kravica. Can you point to Haluge on the map for the Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it close to Hrncici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a village between Hrncici and Konjevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further down, item 7 in its second sentence it says: "Use an all-out attack in combined action with the 2nd JG to destroy the Muslim forces on the axis of attack. Having broken out on to the elevation overlooking Durakovici village create conditions to consolidate the forces of our 3rd -- of our brigade's 3rd Battalion."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could you remind me if we are in open session? If we are, I would kindly ask that we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session, Ms. Vidovic, but of course we shall move for a short while to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back into open session, and Ms. Vidovic is suggesting that we could break now. Yes, indeed. No objection. We will have a 30-minute break starting from now. That means we will start a few minutes before 1.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's continue. By the way, you will recall that yesterday I did mention that I wasn't quite sure what was going to happen on the 6th of December when we were expecting to have a plenary. It has now been decided that we will have a plenary, but due to the fact that Krajisnik and Oric are sitting -- and expecting to sit at quarter to 2.00, the plenary will finish by 1.00. So the sitting that is scheduled for that day will happen. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we left it off at Siljkovici. You stated that one could see the rounds fired with the naked eye. The weapons which were discharged at Siljkovici, how were they positioned in relation to the houses in Siljkovici, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the immediate vicinity of the houses in Siljkovici, some 10 metres away from the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to explain to us some of the consequences of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for a while we'd need to turn into private session. The witness will be mentioning some details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have the usher's assistance in showing the witness a new document. This is a rather large document, Your Honour. For easier bearing with the document, we marked the relevant pages in the order that I will be using them. Wherever you can see the yellow Post-its, those are the pages that I will elicit comments on from the witness. This is a list of personal incomes for November, Bratunac Brigade, bearing the number 01319748 up until 01319804.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, please look at page 1. Can you see it written there "brigade command, Borivoje Tesic, commander." Do you agree with me that this is what it says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to page 2 now. We will dwell on this page for a while. It is stated here: "Mixed artillery battery." Please look at the numbers. Do you agree with me that the list of names starts with number 45 and ends with number 85? Please turn to next page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to this document, therefore, these are some 40-odd persons here. Based on what you observed and experienced in the area where you resided and in view of artillery and other attacks, can you tell us whether the Serb infantry forces in the area had a very strong -- had a very strong artillery support based on the developments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they must have, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the attacks on the areas you described, were these mixed artillery and infantry attacks or did one come before the other? Can you explain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First they started with mortar and artillery attacks, which would then be followed by infantry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to the next page of the document where it says "mixed armoured mechanised unit" listing persons from number 86 through to 142 on the following page. According to this document, there were 66 persons in all. Based on your experience from the area, did the infantry attacks have the support of tanks and APCs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the following page. Persons under number 113 and 116. The person under number 113, Gordana Martic, and under 116, Snezana Martic. Are these female names in our parts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this come to you as a surprise to see that there were women in an armoured mechanised unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not come as a surprise because the two women who got killed in Lolici were also riding in an APC.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we clarify one matter. You say "two women who got killed in Lolici," are you referring to the volunteers for which the document states that they got killed in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the document I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please clarify for the Trial Chamber. Lolici formed part of Sandici, don't they -- doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, one goes from Urkovici through Sandici to reach Lolici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Turn to page 01319752 where it says "air squadron" and there's a list of names there. You've already confirmed this for us, but I will ask you again. Did artillery and infantry attacks also have air support, the ones against your territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Several times in your evidence you said that you came under attack from the Kravica area. Did those units during those attacks have air support as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did have air support.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to page 01319754. Can you find it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is stated "light" -- or rather, "128-millimetre light rocket battery." As far as you know the villages and hamlets of Konjevic Polje, were they targeted by rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by the so-called VBRs, multiple rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to the next page, 01319755, where it says "women volunteers' platoon." You already told us several things about women volunteers. Were there any women volunteers and did you know of them in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 01319757. Do you agree that the document says "1st Infantry Battalion." It says "command" and then "number 1."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will not dwell much on the document, but please look at the last page before the yellow Post-it, 728 Cirkovic Milivoje. Do you agree with me? Could you turn to the last page before the Post-it numbered 2. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, number 728.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Turn the page now where it is stated "list, 2nd Infantry Battalion." Do you agree with me that this 2nd Infantry Battalion list starts with number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the previous page now. Do you agree with me that it ends with number 420.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here -- which page are you referring, the ERN number? Because the previous page, according to me, ends with 728, number 728, Cirkovic Milivoje. 9780 -- so it's not the previous page, so it's a question of translation. 9780 -- the last page then. Yes, the last page of this part of the document, namely the one at ERN 01319780. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The last page of this document or, rather, of the portion of the document which refers to the 2nd Infantry Battalion ends just as you have described it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you found the page 01319781, Witness, which is the next page, where it is stated "3rd Infantry Battalion." I'd like to discuss this now. You have stated on several occasions that this was the Kravica Battalion. Please look at the name under number 1, Mile Milanovic, commander major. Can you tell us again who that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the son of Sveto Milanovic from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the same person who had been elected the president of the SDS in Kravica in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the name below that one, Jovan Nikolic, deputy commander, is that the person you testified about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's Jovan Nikolic, aka Jole.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the name under number 4, Nedjo Nikolic, did you testify about that person as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's Nedjo Nikolic, aka Djedura.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All these persons we have been mentioning now from the command, are they all from Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are all from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 01319796. Look at the number which ends the document, therefore page 01319796, and do you agree that this part of the document ends with number 701 of the 3rd Infantry Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on your experience on the ground and considering the intensity of the attacks coming from the direction of Kravica, do you find it probable that this battalion had around 700 men in the Kravica area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it did have 700 fighters and more because there could have been as many as 1.000 soldiers in the Kravica area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please flip a few pages back, several pages back, and look at page 01319792. Have you found the page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the top third of the document it says "volunteers." Can you see that? Do you agree with me that it starts with number 528 and ends with 565?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document confirm what you were saying that there were volunteers in the Kravica area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we assign an exhibit number to the document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. This document, which consists of pages in Serbo-Croat from 01319748 to 01319804, and therefore 57 pages, together with the corresponding translation thereof into English is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D933.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we put D743 in front of the witness, please. It is a Bratunac Brigade command document dated 10 December 1992 to Drina Corps command signed -- or rather, the name appearing is Borivoje Tesic. The document's number is 04363028.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will quote a part of the document: "The enemy was quiet. No movements of units were observed. "I have relocated part of the units to the Kravica area. I am carrying out preparations according to your order." The date of the document is the 10th of December, 1992. You mentioned several times that you could see certain lines from the villages of the area of Kravica. During December 1992, did you notice that the Serbs brought new fresh forces in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed that they strengthened certain positions amongst those that I could see with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will kindly ask the usher to show the witness another document. This is another Drina Corps command document dated 20 December 1992, the number being 04358063, sent by the Drina Corps command, urgent to the Bratunac Brigade for Lieutenant Colonel Milan Milosevic. I wanted to quote the third paragraph to save some time. "Steer the Krajina Battalion in the Kravica direction" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "You should agree for the 4th Battalion to take over the positions currently held by the Krajina Battalion. Steer the Krajina Battalion in the Kravica direction, and Lieutenant Colonel Tesic will work out the details of its engagement. He will take care of Kravica for the time being so that you can focus on preparing the defence of Bratunac."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, my question to you is: Did you know or hear of the Krajina Battalion in the area of Kravica being active?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you were under the impression, although you've seen the document with about 700 names for the Kravica Battalion, you said that in your estimate there may have been up to 1.000. Did you have any knowledge as to the existence of units from elsewhere to come to the area of Kravica in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had certain knowledge. During their attacks, some of their fighters were left behind and we found IDs on them and we knew that they were from elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your clarification, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we assign an exhibit number to this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document, Ms. Vidovic, which consists of two pages, one in B/C/S, one in English, with ERN 04358063 is being assigned Defence Exhibit Number D934.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe we need to clarify something for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It states here that their fighters were left behind. The way I understood was that some of their fighters were killed and then you would find some documents on their bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They would be killed and they didn't succeed in pulling them out, hence we found the documents and we had proof.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we show another document to the witness, please. It is a Bratunac Brigade command document dated 12 December 1992, the number being 04363033 to Drina Corps command. Your Honours, I would kindly ask that we return to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go into private session for a short while. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this document consisting of two pages, one in B/C/S, one in English, with ERN 04 - this looks to be - 363033 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D935.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness please have a look at D308. These are changes and amendments to the director of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska dated 7 December 1992. The name of General Ratko Mladic appears.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the relevant portion I wanted you to see is to be found on page 00876292.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in English that is page 2. I wanted to quote, that is item 2: "Regardless of the previously determined stages from the directive number 4 of the Corps command, they must execute the following tasks in their areas of responsibility by December 13, 1992: "Keep the existing front line positions; liberate Orasje, Trnovo, Konjevic Polje, Cerska, and Teocak." Witness, this document is dated December 7, 1992. You have discussed December of 1992 previously. Can you remember whether after this date, that is the 7th of December, the area where you lived came under even fiercer attacks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were under attack every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge as to whether the same thing was happening in the area of Mount Glogova and Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Glogova and Cizmici one could hear strong explosions, detonations, and we were able to observe that, or rather, to hear them quite well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have finished with this document. I would kindly ask that another document be put in front of the witness. And I will conclude with this for today, Your Honour. Could you please give the witness a Bratunac Brigade command document sent to the Drina Corps command, attention commander, the number being 04359301.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I wanted to quote this short document to you. It states -- so the date is January 5, 1993. It states: "Given the forthcoming tasks" -- can you see it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Given the forthcoming tasks in the responsibility area of the Corps: "Cleansing of Konjevic Polje and Cerska. "Occupying the front line in front of Bratunac: The village of Jezestica, the village of Pale, Bijela Stijena, Caus, Sase mine, Loznik, the village of Osmace, the village of Medje, the Drina river. "It is necessary that the special brigade stay in the area in responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade in order to execute these tasks. This is why you are to send a request to the RS army Main Staff (General Milovanovic), commander of the East Bosnian Corps." Can you see that the document is dated the 5th of January, 1993, and that it mentions the forthcoming tasks of cleansing of Konjevic Polje and Cerska? Can you see that there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1993 or, to be more precise, around the 5th of January of that year, in that area were you aware of the planning for the cleansing of the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned on several occasions - and I can reiterate - one could see it all with the naked eye. They didn't try to hide because they had nothing to fear. We couldn't target them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is it that you saw exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw infantry columns moving alongside their houses. We could see tanks, APCs next to Milo Milanovic's house. We could see a Howitzer and an anti-aircraft gun at Siljkovici. And above Gornja Brana one could also see a Howitzer. And at Banjevici there was an anti-aircraft gun and a mortar.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the pressure of the Serb forces increase in particular on the 5th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each day was a difficult one, but that one must have been more so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know the existence of this special Serb brigade in the area? Have you -- did you hear of it at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard that there were some special brigades, but we didn't know specific as to what they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of any particular name or a nickname in relation to that special brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at this moment, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we assign an exhibit number to this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document will be given Defence Exhibit Number D936. It consists of two pages, one in Serbo-Croat, one in English, the ERN 04359301. And I think we can stop here for today because it's time up. We will continue tomorrow morning. We are sitting -- you know that we changed the sitting to the morning tomorrow. All right? We'll be sitting tomorrow morning at 9.00. I thank you so much. I take it from what I can guess you'll finish in about an hour tomorrow, something like that, no? First session?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And how much time do you think you require?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I think the Prosecution must reserve the right to take 100 per cent of the time that had been previously allocated for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's meet tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you. Same recommendation as yesterday, Witness. You're not to communicate with anyone on the subject matter of your testimony or the events that you are testifying about in any case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 24th day of November, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.
